text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Nottingham Forest and Liverpool at the City Ground!
Forest start the day sitting just four points above the relegation zone, and they'll be desperate to put some more space between them and the drop.
They've won just two of their 11 games since the start of 2024 (D4 L5), with only one of those victories coming in the league, though that was in their last home match against 10-man West Ham (2-0).
The Tricky Trees come into today on the back of their FA Cup fifth-round exit after conceding a late goal to lose 1-0 to Manchester United.
They can be buoyed by their record against Liverpool though, having never lost a Premier League home match against the Reds (W3 D3).
With Manchester City and Arsenal not playing today, Liverpool can move four points clear at the top of the league ahead of their games.
They've lost just one of their last 17 games in all competitions (W13 D3), though that did come away from home against the Gunners in the Premier League.
The Reds are on a five-match winning run though, following up their EFL Cup victory over Chelsea last weekend with a 3-0 win over Southampton to progress in the FA Cup on Wednesday.
Nuno Espirito Santo makes four changes to the side that started the late defeat against Manchester United on Wednesday.
Sels starts in goal, with Omobamidele, Dominguez and Hudson-Odoi also being brought in.
Turner, Felipe, Danilo and Awoniyi drop to the bench.
Jurgen Klopp makes four changes from their win over Southampton last time out.
Robertson returns from illness, with Konate, Mac Allister and Diaz also coming in to start.
Quansah, Tsimikas, McConnell and Koumas start on the bench.
The Reds are also boosted by the returns of Endo, Szoboszlai and Nunez from injury, and they're also among the substitutes.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Yates gets the game under way for Forest!
Forest win an early corner here and Gibbs-White curls an inviting cross into the middle.
It's cleared as far as Williams by Konate, but he can't pick out a team-mate when he heads it back into the box.
Liverpool are looking to their left to make something happen in the opening stages here, and Robertson has acres of space.
He curls a cross towards Gakpo's run at the far post, but it's just too high for the Dutchman.
Clark knocks it through Yates' legs only to be blocked off by the Forest midfielder.
Van Dijk and Konate are hovering off the back of Toffolo, but Robertson's free-kick is too short for them, and Murillo gets it away.
Elanga races away on a quick break down the left, but when he tries to slide it through to Origi, it's smothered by Konate.
Gibbs-White chases it down when it's knocked back to Kelleher, but the keeper clears his lines in time.
After their 3-0 win at Anfield in October, Liverpool are looking to complete their first league double over Forest since 1984-85 under Joe Fagan.
The hosts win a free-kick on the left, and Gibbs-White tries to be clever by curling it to the front of the crowd and into Yates' path.
He's just caught on his heels slightly, and Kelleher rushes off his line to collect it.
Konate and Dominguez only have eyes for the ball, and the former rises high to clear it but crashes into the Argentinian in the process.
He stays down holding his face, but gets back up without needing treatment.
WIDE! Dominguez sweeps it out to the right for Origi, and he brushes aside Robertson and Gomez as he cuts inside from the wing.
He takes his shot from just outside the D, firing it towards the near post, but it flies just wide.
CLOSE! Robertson makes a driving run down the left before pulling it back to Diaz on the edge of the box.
He aims his shot across goal, but Omobamidele sticks out a leg to block it, and his deflection is just wide of the near post.
Liverpool are starting to up the pressure here, with Robertson still being given a lot of space down the left.
He curls an inviting cross into the six-yard box, and it looks like Sels has it covered, but Murillo hooks it clear just in front of him.
Dominguez fires a ball through midfield looking for Origi, who is hovering between the centre-backs.
Van Dijk has it covered though, and Liverpool are back in possession.
GREAT SAVE! Forest smother Liverpool's latest attack before they surge forward on the counter.
Elanga gets in between Van Dijk and Konate to get into the box, but Kelleher rushes out and sticks out a leg to keep out his low strike.
CHANCE! It's Clark who cuts inside from the left this time, and a pocket of space just opens up for him.
He whips a shot towards the far top corner, but it's just too high as it flies over.
BLOCK! Bradley plays a good one-two with Elliott to get away down the right before he pulls it back into the box, but it's behind Diaz.
Clark reacts quickest to reach it but scuffs his shot to the Colombian.
He pokes it on goal from close range, but Murillo throws himself in front of it to send it behind.
Hudson-Odoi does well against Bradley as he pushes forward down the left, and he has bodies to aim for in the middle when he gets away from the youngster.
Van Dijk gets to it first though, and calmly nods it back to Kelleher.
Diaz is starting to cause Forest some real problems as he drifts out to the right this time.
He fizzes a low ball across the face of goal on the half-turn, but none of his team-mates are there to get what would've been a tap-in.
Gomez has had a couple of late fouls in the last couple of minutes, with his latest bringing Gibbs-White down as the midfielder swept it out to Hudson-Odoi.
The referee pulls it back for a free-kick, but Forest can't do anything with it.
Gibbs-White's throughball is straight against Gomez, but Murillo gets across to tidy up before he can counter.
The defender goes long for Elanga, but shows too much of it to Kelleher, giving the winger no chance.
Yates slides in with a well-timed tackle on Mac Allister, and Dominguez tries to catch Liverpool out with an early throughball in behind.
Elanga was standing offside though, and as soon as he starts to chase it, the flag goes up.
Liverpool are still dominating possession here, with 73 per cent of the ball so far.
They're slowing things down at the moment though and knocking it around in their own half.
Bradley floats a lovely ball over the top for Gakpo to latch onto, and instead of going for goal, he tries to cushion it back to Elliott on the edge of the box.
He can't get close to it though, and Omobamidele comfortably clears.
Toffolo manages to cut out Bradley's attack this time, and his first thought is to play it down the line for Elanga.
He's tracked all the way by Mac Allister though, and can only win a throw-in.
Origi wriggles out of a tight spot on the left and manages to poke it through to Dominguez on the left of the box.
He can't get hold of his shot properly, and his tame effort rolls wide of the far post.
HALF-TIME: NOTTINGHAM FOREST 0-0 LIVERPOOL.
It's goalless at the break between Forest and Liverpool.
The Reds dominated in the first half and got into some good positions, but despite all of that, they never managed a shot on target.
Diaz saw two great chances blocked, while Clark whipped a shot just over the bar, but otherwise, it's been a fairly quiet game for Sels.
At the other end, former Liverpool man, Origi, fired an effort wide of the near post 15 minutes in before Kelleher made a huge save with his foot to deny Elanga after a quick break.
Klopp didn't look too happy on the sidelines, and given that his side have struggled at times in the final third, it's no surprise.
All season, Liverpool have improved in the second half, and their manager will be urging them for more here as well.
Forest may not have created much, but they had the best chance of the game.
They're always a threat on the counter, but they need to take those chances when they come.
Liverpool get us back under way for the second half!
It's an open start to the first half, with Dominguez seeing a shot blocked at one end before Liverpool move it quickly the other way.
Diaz clips it to the far post for Clark, but he has it taken off his toe by Murillo.
CHANCE! Diaz can't make contact for a shot, but he manages to scuff it out to the left of the box, where Robertson is making a late run.
He puts his laces through the half-volley, hitting it across goal, but a deft touch from Omobamidele takes it wide.
After a bright start by Forest, Liverpool are starting to regain their foothold here.
They're moving it upfield quickly, but Forest are standing their ground whenever the Reds get it into the box at the moment.
Bradley and Elliott link up well down the right, but Toffolo makes a good block to stop the latter's cross from going into the box.
Clark tries to recycle it, but he's shepherded out of play by Murillo.
Forest are sitting very deep in their own half, so even when they do win the ball back, there's no way out for them.
Yates sends a hopeful long ball forward, but Elanga can't get anywhere near it, so Liverpool start again.
Liverpool's latest corner swings away from everyone, bouncing out to Elliott on the edge of the box.
He lets it bounce before hitting a shot on goal, but Yates blocks it with his head and needs a moment before getting back to his feet.
The first yellow card of the game is shown to Robertson, who crashes into Williams in his attempt to keep the Liverpool attack alive.
That booking was Robertson's last involvement in the game as he's the first to go off in a double change for the Reds.
Nunez replaces him.
And Clark is also taken off, with Endo also making a return from injury in his place.
Diaz gets away from Omobamidele with a clever drop of the shoulder and drives to the byline.
He gets his head up to look for a team-mate, but that gives Williams the chance to slide in and dispossess him.
WIDE! It's worked neatly from right to left by Liverpool with one-touch passes, and Diaz threads it through for Nunez.
The angle is against him, but he still drills a low shot on goal, only to fire it into the side netting.

events.action: fire it into the side net

text: The first change for Forest sees Origi taken off, with both sets of fans giving him a warm ovation on his way off the pitch.
Awoniyi, who scored the winner in this exact fixture last season, replaces him.
SO CLOSE! Forest break quickly on the counter once more, with Hudson-Odoi sliding it into the box for Awoniyi.
He has Konate tight to his back, so he cushions it into Toffolo instead.
His cross lands at Elanga's feet, but he sends his first-time shot just wide of the far post.
Elliott's corner is curled straight into Sels' gloves, and he goes long for Hudson-Odoi on the left.
He knocks it into Awoniyi on the edge of the box, but he takes too long to get a shot away, and Bradley shields it back to Kelleher.
WIDE! Williams is caught on the ball on halfway, and Nunez bursts through the middle before switching it out to Gakpo on the right.
The Uruguayan continues his run and wants it back, but Gakpo goes it alone, firing into the side netting.
Elanga takes it off Gomez's toe on the edge of the area, but Mac Allister wins it back before chipping a lovely ball over the top.
Nunez peels away to get a glancing touch on it, but he can't direct it on target.
Klopp isn't happy with the free-kick that's been given against his side, and he's making it clear to the fourth official.
The referee also comes across and manages to calm him down.
CHANCE! Diaz thinks about putting in a cross but instead carries it along the edge of the box before whipping a shot on goal.
It's always swerving away from the target though, and it flies wide.
Liverpool's third change sees another player coming back from injury as Szoboszlai comes on in place of Elliott.
Dominguez has gone down a couple of times in the second half, and he's on the floor holding his thigh once more.
It doesn't look like he's going to be able to carry on this time.
Dominguez is helped halfway off the field by Yates before the physio takes over, with the midfielder limping along.
Danilo comes on in his place.
SAVE! It's a lovely first-time pass from Danilo down the left to pick out Hudson-Odoi's run into the box, and he drags it past Bradley to get a sight of goal.
He scuffs at the shot though, and it's a comfortable save for Kelleher.
There are big shouts for a penalty from the Liverpool fans and players as they're claiming that Hudson-Odoi blocked Szoboszlai's shot with his arm.
The winger's back was turned, and that's where it hit him, so it's just a corner.
Liverpool's final roll of the dice is a double one.
Danns, who scored two goals after coming off the bench in the win over Southampton in midweek, replaces Gakpo.
And Bradley is also taken off, with Tsimikas on for him.
Sels comes off his line to collect a cross and Danns crashes into him as he tries to get on the end of it.
The goalkeeper stays down, and the youngster goes into the book.
Sels needs treatment after that collision with Danns, and it seems to be a problem with his thigh.
The medical team are on, but they've been seeing to him for a long time.
Sels slowly gets back to his feet, and it looks like he is going to carry on.
Turner is getting warmed up on the sidelines, but for now, he isn't going to be needed.
Omobamidele sells himself trying to block Endo's throughball, but it rolls past him straight out to Diaz.
He cuts inside from the left before whipping a shot across goal which is deflected out for a corner.
GOOD CHANCE! We're into a minimum of eight minutes of stoppage time here and Liverpool are still throwing everything they have at Forest.
Diaz fizzes a dangerous low cross into the six-yard box, but Nunez can't reach it on the stretch as he slides in.
The referee deems that Gibbs-White is taking too long over a corner kick, so he's booked for time-wasting.
The yellow card is out once again, this time for Danilo, who is also booked for time-wasting.
GREAT SAVE! Tsimikas whips Liverpool's latest corner into the box and it's just too high for Nunez and hits Murillo behind him.
The defender doesn't know much about it as his header bounces towards goal, but Sels reflexively sticks out his arm to keep it out on the line.
BLOCK! Forest break quickly on the counter once more, with Hudson-Odoi striding down the left before sweeping a cross to the edge of the box.
Gibbs-White has space for a shot, which he takes, but Van Dijk sticks out a leg to deflect it wide.
Szoboszlai's throughball to Endo is too heavy, and Danilo puts his laces through the clearance, just wanting to get it away.
Liverpool quickly work it back into the final third to win a late corner, which is likely going to be their final chance.
NUNEZ WINS IT FOR LIVERPOOL! In the dying seconds of the game, the Reds snatch a victory! Tsimikas latches onto the initial corner and volleys a shot on goal which Gibbs-White blocks.
Forest just can't clear their lines though and Mac Allister nicks it off Hudson-Odoi before floating a lovely cross into the far post.
Nunez rises above Williams to meet it and glances his header past Sels and into the bottom corner.
1-0 Liverpool!
Mac Allister was the calmest person in the City Ground as he held off Hudson-Odoi on the edge of the box before spinning into space to pick out a perfect cross.
Felipe isn't happy with the referee, and he's crossed a line with his complaints.
He picks up a late booking for dissent.
FULL-TIME: NOTTINGHAM FOREST 0-1 LIVERPOOL.
Liverpool win their first-ever Premier League game away at Forest, with Nunez heading in a late winner to give the Reds a 1-0 victory.

The visitors dominated throughout but failed to have a shot on target in the first half, with Forest having the best chance before the break, with Kelleher making a great stop to keep out Elanga after a quick counter.
Liverpool upped the pressure in the second half, with Robertson seeing a shot cleared off the line before Diaz and Nunez both went close.
In the ninth minute of stoppage time, Mac Allister picked out Nunez with a lovely ball, and the substitute glanced in the winner to seal a big three points.
It means that Liverpool go four points clear at the top of the table, with Manchester City and Arsenal not playing until later on this weekend.
Next up for them is their Europa League round of 16 first leg against Sparta Prague.
Forest stay in 17th, still four points above the drop zone.
They travel to Brighton next weekend.
That's all for today, goodbye!
